  - Windows (via reusable-windows.yml)
  - macOS (via reusable-macos.yml)
  - Ubuntu / Linux (via reusable-ubuntu.yml and sanitizer jobs, etc.)
  - Android (via reusable-android job in the reusable suite; referenced from build.yml)
  - iOS (via reusable-ios or equivalent mobile job; referenced from build.yml)
  - Emscripten / WebAssembly (via reusable-emscripten.yml)
  - WASI (via reusable-wasi.yml)
  - Additional sanitizer configurations (via reusable-san.yml) running on Linux

  These OSes are configured as separate jobs rather than a single matrix field; each job uses its own runs-on and calls the appropriate reusable-*.yml.

  - The main Tests workflow does not declare a single global python-version matrix in build.yml. - File path
  - .github/workflows/reusable-docs.yml

- Workflow name
  - name: Reusable Docs

  - on:

    - workflow_dispatch:
    - push:
      - branches:

        - '3.*'
      - paths:
        - 'Doc/pylock.toml'
        - 'Doc/requirements.txt'
        - '.github/workflows/reusable-docs.yml'

- Declared permissions
  - permissions:
    - contents: read

- Operating system and tests within the docs workflow
  This is a reusable documentation workflow with several jobs:

  1) build-doc
     - runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     - Sets up Python and builds the HTML documentation.
     - Key commands (test/build commands):
       - Install build dependencies:
         - make -C Doc/ venv
       - Build HTML documentation (with nitpicky warnings):
         - make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python \
             SPHINXOPTS="--quiet --nitpicky --warning-file sphinx-warnings.txt" html
       - Check warnings (on pull_request):
         - python Doc/tools/check-warnings.py \
             --annotate-diff "${branch_base}" "${branch_pr}" \
             --fail-if-regression \
             --fail-if-improved \
             --fail-if-new-news-nit
       - Collect HTML IDs (on pull_request):
         - python Doc/tools/check-html-ids.py collect Doc/build/html -o Doc/build/html-ids-head.json.gz

  2) check-html-ids

     - needs: build-doc
     - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
     - uses: ./.github/workflows/reusable-check-html-ids.yml
     - This job reuses another workflow; its detailed commands are in reusable-check-html-ids.yml, not in reusable-docs.yml itself.

  3) doctest
     - name: 'Doctest'
     - runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
     - Key commands (test commands):
       - Install dependencies:
         - sudo ./.github/workflows/posix-deps-apt.sh && sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends wamerican
       - Configure CPython:
         - ./configure --with-pydebug
       - Build CPython:
         - make -j4
       - Install build dependencies for docs:
         - make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python venv
       - Run documentation doctest (the main docs test command in this job):
         - xvfb-run make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python SPHINXERRORHANDLING="--fail-on-warning" doctest

  4) check-epub
     - name: 'Check EPUB'
     - runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     - Key commands:
       - Install build dependencies and epubcheck:
         - make -C Doc/ venv
         - python -m pip install epubcheck
       - Build EPUB documentation:
         - make -C Doc/ PYTHON=../python epub
       - Run epubcheck (docs validation command):
         - epubcheck Doc/build/epub/Python.epub &> Doc/epubcheck.txt
       - Show epubcheck output:
         - cat Doc/epubcheck.txt
       - Check for fatal errors in EPUB:
         - python Doc/tools/check-epub.py

  - In job build-doc and check-epub:
